question: Under a listed family of 60 laws that use no names (takes of a sole candidate with recorded rations and treatments, three owing rations and one new treatment, each added by hand), on eight small starts: do two parts the growth made meet only through knots the growth made; is one such knot a knot both parts descend from; and does the course of one part then differ between the other part usable and barred, attributed through their meeting? Which listed laws are the least for each?
inputs: The family of laws with its controls, the starts with the unsymmetric ring, the renamings, the bounds, the guard's limits and the order of runs named in the pre-registration and its four data files; this ticket's definitions and claim; ticket A's definitions; the frozen definitions of the copier study's first two tickets, of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001 and the shared definitions of RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001; the engine of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001A and ticket A's engine, unchanged, read-only, for the gate.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; for the engine's author, the drafter's scratch prototype and anything it produced beyond what the pre-registration and its data files disclose; any change to a frozen engine; any rule added so that a pattern reads; any law, start or renaming left out after its outcome is seen.
primary_observable: For every law, knot law, start and ordered pair of parts wholly apart after rounds 1 to 4: the meeting round, the linking set with each linking knot's round and each linking distinction's holders, whether the meeting is only through made knots (strict form), whether a linking knot is an ancestral common knot made by births, the course from the first part only with the second usable and barred in canonical form, the attribution of the first differing used value, and the knot test as registered; per law the three verdicts and, over the family, the minimal laws among the listed laws for each.
comparators_or_controls: No taking rule (no meeting, by argument); a rule that looks at parts as the positive control; ticket A's planted case, classed 'through a start knot'; four ration controls and a comparison of one bit on the ring starts; an unsymmetric ring with no prediction and no scratch run; renamings of the starts; the guard's limits multiplied by 10 and 100 where it stopped.
resource_budget: One cap for the whole ticket: 70 minutes of wall time on at most 6 processes, each under a memory cap; bounds by counts (7 rounds, a stop after the first round leaving more than 1,500 knots, and the guard's limits as written). What a cut leaves is a prefix of the registered order and is reported as not run.
first_executable_signal: The gate: ticket A's 648 runs against the fold engine, the listing of the data file reproduced birth by birth, ticket A's attribution records classed as registered; then the negative, positive and planted controls.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' entry; arguments, replications of the scratch runs and reported readings are marked as such. A dependence counts only where attribution is accepted and every tested knot passes; a differing pair whose barred run was not knot-tested is undecided.
stop_rule: Stop when every registered run within the cap is done and each of the three verdicts is decided for every law reached, with the minimal laws among the listed laws (or among the laws run) reported as a set.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of eight small starts built by hand, to seven rounds, over a listed family of laws; every new rule, the starts, the bars and the readings are supplied. Everything predicted was seen in the drafter's scratch runs except attribution and the unsymmetric ring. The expected dependence is one count handed over at a meeting that a made knot links, which is also whether the parts meet at all: not a pattern reading anything, nothing composed over several births, and not a fold of emergence. 'Least' is among the listed laws only. No claim about living things, minds, physics or time.
